clue.text: 23's sixth sense welcomed by confused Highland guide

definitions.note: the clue at 23 is a trumpeter's name, so this means 'a trumpeter is'

parts.note: dizzy means muddled or confused

indicators.note: the guide takes the sense in as a host welcomes a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a gillie is a Scottish attendant who guides anglers and stalkers
ESP, extrasensory perception, is the so-called sixth sense

explanation.surface: A muddled Scottish guide appears to have a sixth sense.
explanation.walkthrough: '23' points to the answer at 23-across, a word for a horn player, and the 's reads as 'is'. 'confused' looks like a description of the guide but supplies the nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The jazz trumpeter of that nickname is a famous example of a horn player.

clue.text: Vibrant — as is Bronze Star?

definitions.meaning: the phrase Bronze Star has the letters Z, E, S, T running across its two words, so it is full of that word for gusto

explanation.surface: Is a military medal something lively?
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as ZEST-FUL: 'bronZE STar' contains ZEST, so the phrase is full of zest. The question mark flags the wordplay-style definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of gusto and enthusiasm is vibrant, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Even the setter's a hirsute specimen

parts.note: even, as in 'even now', means yet
the setter refers to themselves as I; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: The setter admits to being rather hairy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Abominable Snowman is a legendary shaggy creature, so it is a hairy specimen.

clue.text: Hot inside island church on river, but cold in here!

indicators.note: the hot letter is placed inside the run of island, church and river
in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next, so church comes before river

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
the Ouse is an English river, here the Yorkshire one
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A warm church on a river island contrasts with a chilly store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' and 'cold' look like opposites in one scene; 'Hot' just gives a single letter to place inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional building for storing ice is a place where it is cold, as the exclamation hints.

clue.text: Latitude with fish turning up on journey

indicators.note: in a down clue the turned fish sits on top of the journey
in a down clue the fish reads upwards, so its letters go in reverse

parts.note: an eel is a fish
a way is a route or journey

explanation.surface: A fish turns up on a voyage at some latitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses EEL to give LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude in the sense of freedom or room to manoeuvre is a synonym.

clue.text: Sewer displaying strain under main motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue the strain sits below the main and the motorway

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the sea
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1
stress means strain or pressure

explanation.surface: A drain shows strain beneath a main road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sewer' wants to be a drain, but it is one who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who sews for a living is a sewer in the needle-and-thread sense.

clue.text: Denounce little devil to everyone

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
each means every one

explanation.surface: Someone condemns a little devil to all and sundry.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a public official with misconduct is to accuse or denounce them.

clue.text: Source of problems in cruise-line bars at sea, with old getting cross

parts.note: P&O is a British shipping and cruise company, written here as P AND O

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Trouble aboard a cruise as an old passenger gets angry at the bars.
explanation.walkthrough: P&O is a well-known British cruise line. 'at sea' rearranges BARS as RASB.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the jar opened by Pandora released all the world's ills, so it is a source of troubles.

clue.text: Satire we deployed, in a way

indicators.note: deployed means arranged or set out, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: We used satire, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means so to speak or in a manner of speaking, a synonym for in a way.

clue.text: Gallop ahead — odds incidental in the beginning

indicators.note: the odd letters are treated as unimportant and dropped, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: A horse gallops ahead in the opening, with the betting odds unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: Racing words disguise the instruction: drop the odd letters of 'Gallop ahead' and keep the evens.
explanation.definitionFit: The first Greek letter stands for the start, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: Parking Lycra kit, he rectified itching

indicators.note: rectified means put right, so these letters are reset in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sorted out a Lycra sports kit that made him itch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rash caused by heat and blocked sweat ducts, causing irritation of the skin.

clue.text: Trump's neckwear

definitions.meaning: to trump is to play a trump card; the 's stands for 'is'
a frilled collar worn in Elizabethan times

explanation.surface: A comment on a politician's taste in collars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trump' looks like the politician, but it is the card-game verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge or whist, to play a trump on another suit is this; it is also an Elizabethan pleated collar.

clue.text: Amazonian region?

parts.note: the Amazons of Greek myth were a race of women warriors, so their territory would admit no males

explanation.surface: A part of the Amazon basin in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazonian' suggests the rainforest, but it means the women warriors of myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally means disputed ground between armies; here it is read literally as a place free of males.

clue.text: CIA worried about suspect ring being origin of conflict

indicators.note: the shuffled agency letters go around the other pieces
worried means agitated, so these three letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
sus is informal shorthand for suspect
to ring is to bell, a bell being what rings

explanation.surface: The CIA frets over a suspect ring that sparked a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a gang of plotters but is the verb for sounding a bell; the shuffled agency letters go around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase names an act or event that justifies or provokes war.

clue.text: Break-up of band aborted quietly, somewhere around London

indicators.note: aborted means cut short, so the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a collar is a band round the neck
P, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quietly
SE, the South East, is the region of England around London

explanation.surface: A pop group splits up after quietly ending a tour around London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a pop group but is a collar.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakdown or failure of something is a synonym for a falling apart.

clue.text: Jeffrey's one used to taking a bow

definitions.meaning: Jeffrey ... is a British novelist and former Conservative politician; the 's stands for 'is'

definitions.text: one used to taking a bow
definitions.meaning: someone who shoots with a bow

explanation.surface: Jeffrey is used to applause on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a bow' suggests applause, but it is the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeffrey's surname is shared with a person who shoots arrows from a bow.

clue.text: Lacking structure, let out class

parts.note: to free is to let out or release
a form is a school class

explanation.surface: An unstructured lesson as the class is released.
explanation.definitionFit: Art or verse without fixed rules or pattern is described as unconstrained by convention.

clue.text: Useful chemical features endless stimuli when shaken

indicators.note: shaken means stirred up, so these letters are jumbled
the word stimuli loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A chemical that works well when shaken provides stimuli.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the I of 'stimuli', and 'when shaken' rearranges STIMUL.
explanation.definitionFit: This dye indicator turns red in acid and blue in alkali, handy in the lab.

clue.text: 'Tempest' failing on the road, male drops out

indicators.note: failing means breaking down, so the remaining letters are jumbled
the male letters are removed from the road phrase before the shuffle

parts.note: he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A car named Tempest breaks down on the road and the driver leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops out' removes HE from ON THE ROAD, and 'failing' rearranges ONTROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating windstorm is a kind of tempest.

clue.text: Time to position article from Paris — on these?

definitions.note: the clue as a whole suggests that something, a table top, is positioned on them

parts.note: to rest something is to place or position it
les is the French plural definite article

explanation.surface: It is time to set out a French object on supports.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: the article positioned 'on these' implies the supports themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Frames with sloping legs support a board such as a table top, so things are placed on them.

clue.text: Pain when deadheading sea pink?

indicators.note: deadheading a plant removes its spent head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: plumbago is a genus of plants that includes the sea pinks

explanation.surface: A gardener feels a pang while deadheading flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Gardening terms hide the instruction to drop the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ache in the lower back is a specific kind of pain.

clue.text: Flat out, with pet sadly carried off in stages

indicators.note: carried off means taken away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: prostrate means lying flat out
the letters of pet taken in a disordered form, so they can be lifted out of the flat word in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone lies flat out after their pet is sadly taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' turns PET into P...TE, the order in which those letters are removed by 'carried off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Platforms for speakers are raised stages, the Latin plural of rostrum.

clue.text: That woman embracing low-born flying officer in fiction

indicators.note: the pronoun wraps around the scrambled letters

parts.note: her refers to that woman

indicators.note: flying means moving about wildly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman embraces a lowly born airman in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying officer' suggests the RAF, but 'flying' is the anagram signal and the officer is a naval one from C. S. Forester's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio of that name is C. S. Forester's fictional Royal Navy officer.

clue.text: Ham uncovered brief evidence

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters are stripped away

parts.note: gammon is cured ham

explanation.surface: A ham is exposed by short evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' strips the G and N from GAMMON. The definition is the short form of ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts used to support an argument are called ammunition, shortened to this informal word.

clue.text: Duck out of soggy film

indicators.note: the duck letter is taken out of the damp word

parts.note: moist means damp or soggy
a duck is zero in cricket, written O

explanation.surface: A duck emerges from a soggy movie.

clue.text: One may be drawn discreetly, we hear, to be of use

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: you draw a veil over something to keep it discreetly hidden

explanation.surface: Something drawn discreetly turns out to be useful.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to help or serve, synonymous with being useful.

clue.text: Very warm current crossing river

indicators.note: the river letter crosses into the middle of the current word

parts.note: topical means current, of present interest

explanation.surface: A warm current flows across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' suggests a flow of water, but it means up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot, humid climates such as those near the equator are described this way.

clue.text: Most singular or eccentric 23

definitions.note: the answer at 23-across is a word for one who plays a horn

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so these letters are reordered
